newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark steadies in Europe after overnight moves.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark steadies in Europe after overnight moves.

text.p: The dollar was firm against the mark in morning Europe though off fresh overnight highs, underpinned by Asian currency turbulence, sterling/mark gains and the mark's ongoing general weakness on its European crosses.
But there was little fresh news overnight and in early Europe to drive the dollar higher and dealers said volume was fairly thin as European markets assessed overnight moves.

"It's all noise and no volume at the moment," said Nick Parsons, forex strategist at Paribas in London. "After the explosive move late Friday in New York and the exaggerated action in Asia, the market's trying to take stock right now."
The ongoing turbulence in Asian currencies, which saw new lows overnight in the Philippine peso, Malaysian ringitt and Thai baht, helped underpin the dollar said dealers.
"The dollar is the vehicle currency in Asia and will be supported as long as the speculators attack the local currencies," said a U.S. bank dealer here.

Furthermore, the appetite for Asian central banks to sell dollars to stem their currencies' depreciation appears to have waned with Malaysia's Bank of Negara only making a half-hearted attempt to stand in the way of the speculators, said dealers.
By 0830 GMT, dollar/mark stood at 1.7815/20 marks, down from its near six-year high of 1.7845 seen in New York on Friday but still above Friday's late European level of 1.7700/10 marks.

Dealers said the market was cautious of possible comments from the G7 to stem the pace of dollar/mark's latest climb but were mindful that last week's mark positive comments from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer only proved a temporary cap for dollar gains.
"Dollar/mark is likely to be choppy and volatitle as we may see G7 statements become more threatening," said Paribas' Parsons.
But the market is gravitating towards the round-figure 1.80 marks and dealers said it may take more than just verbal intervention to interrupt its path to that target.

Dollar gains have so far depended on external factors. The U.S. interest rate outlook remains subdued and U.S. retail sales and CPI data later this week are expected to confirm that. "U.S. rate expectations are dropping sharply and when the Asian currency turmoil starts to die down, we should see the dollar slip back against the mark," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International.

Sterling/mark's gains to 3.0140 overnight, its highest level since October 1990, also provided some dollar/mark support. Expectations of higher UK interest rates after last week's 25 basis point rise continue to prop the pound.
By 0900, the pound stood at 3.0110/20 from 2.9985/95 marks late Friday in Europe.

Dollar/yen, meantime, occupied familiar ranges in the mid-113 region, trading at 113.56/66 from 113.84/89 late Friday. Mark/yen's morning decline to a fresh 23-month low of 63.68 kept a lid on dollar/yen, said dealers.
